title: Fault-tolerant quantum computing with a microwave Cat Bus
authors: Yanyan Chen, Xinyang Yu, Yueyang Min, Zhihao Zhang, Shuaifan Cao, Xiaopeng Li
abstract: The scalability of fault-tolerant neutral-atom quantum computers is constrained by the latency of shuttling with optical tweezers, imposing a stringent trade-off between qubit overhead and circuit depth in quantum algorithm compilation. Here we propose a hardware-efficient, shuttling-free architecture that achieves all-to-all connectivity. Remote Rydberg atoms are resonantly entangled through a microwave ``Cat Bus''---a cavity mode autonomously stabilized in a bosonic cat state. The Cat Bus natively supports the highly parallelized execution of one-to-many $\mathrm{CZ}^n$ gates with exponentially suppressed crosstalk. We derive the resulting cat--atom error channel from the underlying interactions and physical constraints. For fault-tolerant operation, we develop a hardware-aware scheduling scheme that exploits the native cat--atom $\mathrm{CZ}^{n}$ gate to construct a syndrome-extraction circuit with minimum depth. We benchmark the architecture using hypergraph-product (HGP) codes and estimate a 180-fold reduction in syndrome-extraction cycle time at $N=10^5$ data qubits compared with an atom-rearrangement-based architecture. Under matched two-qubit depolarizing noise, the corresponding error threshold increases from $0.55\%$ to $0.72\%$. Under the hardware-derived error model, we obtain a threshold of $0.80\%$, corresponding to a threshold cooperativity of $C_{\mathrm{th}}=7.8 \times 10^4$, compatible with experimentally accessible parameters for Rydberg-coupled microwave-cavity systems. By avoiding atom transport, the Cat Bus provides a route towards high-speed, fault-tolerant neutral-atom quantum computation.
summary: The paper proposes a microwave 'Cat Bus' architecture to solve the latency bottleneck in scaling neutral-atom quantum computers. By using cavity modes stabilized as bosonic cat states, it achieves shuttling-free all-to-all connectivity and implements fast, high-fidelity one-to-many entangling gates. This results in significant improvements in syndrome extraction speed and error thresholds for fault-tolerant computation.
main_problem: The primary challenge addressed is overcoming the latency bottleneck associated with shuttling atoms in neutral-atom quantum computers to achieve scalable, fault-tolerant operation with all-to-all connectivity.
main_result: The proposed Cat Bus architecture enables a 180-fold reduction in syndrome-extraction cycle time compared to atom rearrangement methods and increases the error threshold from 0.55% to 0.72% under depolarizing noise.
method: The authors develop hardware-aware scheduling schemes for syndrome extraction, benchmarking performance using Hypergraph-Product (HGP) codes against various noise models.
model_or_system: The system is a hybrid platform coupling neutral atoms trapped in a static 2D optical lattice with superconducting microwave cavities forming a 'Cat Bus.' This bus mediates entanglement via bosonic cat states, enabling shuttling-free all-to-all connectivity.
key_observables: Syndrome-extraction cycle time (180x reduction), error threshold (0.72% to 0.80%), and logical failure rate (LFR).
important_parameters: Cat amplitude ($\alpha$), cooperativity ($C$), physical error rates ($p$), and system size ($N=10^5$ data qubits).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the large-amplitude limit for cat states, assuming leading errors are dominated by cat Z errors and atomic leakage.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the shuttling-free processor geometry (crossed-chip setup) and show error characterization of the native CZ gate, including infidelity vs. amplitude ($\alpha$) and optimized infidelity vs. cooperativity ($C$).
paper_structure: The paper first introduces the Cat Bus mechanism for all-to-all connectivity via a one-to-many CZ gate. It then derives the error channel and proposes hardware-aware scheduling for syndrome extraction using HGP codes, concluding with performance benchmarks comparing cycle times and error thresholds against existing methods.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses scalability in neutral-atom quantum computing by proposing a novel, high-speed interconnect (the Cat Bus) that bypasses slow physical atom movement, which is crucial for realizing large-scale fault tolerance.
